description:
## What
Add 5 private matching functions in pkix-path/src/lib.rs that test whether a GeneralName (from a subject's SAN or DN) satisfies a GeneralSubtree constraint.

## Algorithm

### name_matches_subtree(name, subtree) -> bool
Dispatch to variant-specific matcher. Return false for mismatched variants.

### matches_directory_name(subject_dn, constraint_dn) -> bool
Call existing name_matches() (or ava_values_match chain). Exact match only (RFC 5280 §7.1 normalisation).

### matches_dns_name(subject: &str, constraint: &str) -> bool
- If constraint has leading dot: subject must end with constraint (label-aware suffix)
  e.g. ".example.com" matches "foo.example.com" but NOT "example.com" itself
- If no leading dot: exact match only
- Case-insensitive ASCII comparison

### matches_rfc822_name(subject: &str, constraint: &str) -> bool
- If constraint contains '@': exact match
- If constraint starts with '.': local@domain must have domain suffix matching constraint
- Otherwise: domain part of subject must equal constraint (case-insensitive)

### matches_uri(subject_uri: &str, constraint: &str) -> bool
- Extract host from URI (between :// and first / or end)
- Apply DNS matching rules to host vs constraint

### matches_ip_address(subject_bytes: &[u8], constraint_bytes: &[u8]) -> bool
- constraint_bytes must be 8 bytes (IPv4) or 32 bytes (IPv6) — addr+mask pairs
- Split into addr and mask halves
- Each byte: (subject[i] & mask[i]) == (constraint_addr[i] & mask[i])
- Return false if lengths don't match expected sizes

## Defensive programming
- Return false (not error) for constraint variants not yet handled (URI, IP) if out of scope
- DNS: reject empty labels, label must not start/end with hyphen (RFC 952)
- All string comparisons: lowercase before comparing

## Acceptance criteria
- DNS: ".example.com" matches "sub.example.com", rejects "example.com" and "notexample.com"
- DNS: "example.com" matches only "example.com"
- RFC822: "@example.com" in constraint matches only that address; ".example.com" matches any @*.example.com
- IP: 192.168.0.0/255.255.0.0 matches 192.168.5.10, rejects 10.0.0.1
- No panics on empty or malformed input
title: Implement GeneralName matching functions
